headline: Fueled by 'electric' MSG crowd, resurgent Rangers improve to 6-0-0 on home ice
take:
Per ESPN, the Rangers beat the Anaheim Ducks 5-2 on Monday at Madison Square Garden to move to 6-0-0 at home, matching the second-longest season-opening home winning streak in franchise history.

The numbers suggest the Rangers have been a solid team but not a dominant one. They have 52.8 percent of the expected goals so far this season, which measures the quality of chances each side creates and puts them modestly ahead of their opponents. At five-on-five, that share is 51 percent, so the edge is thin. What stands out is how they have gotten results. The Rangers have scored 4.3 fewer goals than their chances would predict, meaning their shooters have underperformed, while their goaltending has saved 6.9 more goals than expected given the shots faced. That pairing points to goaltending carrying a good share of the 6-3-1 record. The penalty kill is a real strength, allowing just 0.51 expected goals per game. Anaheim, at 49.1 percent, has been close to even and is doing the opposite, getting 2.4 goals saved above expected from its goalies while its finishing has lagged.
